quotes.text: The real block is that operational systems and analytical systems aren't wired to work as one.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the structural root cause behind export-driven reporting.

quotes.text: Dynamics three sixty five keeps doing what it's best at, recording the truth as it happens. Fabric continuously shapes that truth into a form that can be visualized and acted on, and Powerbi becomes the lens that shows those insights right inside the workflow.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clearly assigns each product its role in the event-to-insight pipeline.

quotes.text: A beautiful Powerbi dashboard isn't worth much if it lives in a forgotten browser tab. The value isn't in how good it looks. It's in how many decisions it influences
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for embedding reports where decisions are made.

quotes.text: Designing separate reports for each major role means you control the signal to noise ratio from the start.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Actionable design advice for role-specific embedded reports.

quotes.text: A sales slump caught in the third week of the month can still be turned around. The same slump identified after month end is just used to explain why the target was missed.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Illustrates the business value of reducing insight latency.

takeaways: Exporting Dynamics 365 data to Excel creates stale, conflicting snapshots because operational and analytical systems are not wired together.
Pointing Microsoft Fabric at Dataverse, shaping the data with Data Factory or Dataflow Gen2 and securing it with role-based access creates a live analytical copy without middleware.
Role-specific Power BI reports embedded in Dynamics 365 forms cut insight latency from days to minutes and drive adoption because they sit inside the daily workflow.
hook: If your team still exports Dynamics 365 data to Excel to build charts, the numbers are stale before the meeting starts. This episode is for Dynamics 365, Power BI and data platform professionals who want live analytics inside the apps people already use. You will learn how to connect Dynamics 365 to Microsoft Fabric and embed role-specific Power BI reports for real-time decisions.
